stem: A 34-year-old man has CT of the abdomen for a kidney stone. He has never had abdominal trauma or surgery. Besides a normal spleen, CT shows three round 1-cm nodules beside the splenic hilum that enhance exactly like the spleen, and scintigraphy shows that they take up the tracer for splenic tissue.
oneliner: 34M + no trauma or surgery + normal spleen + three 1-cm nodules at the splenic hilum enhancing like spleen + spleen-tracer uptake → which developmental event?
ask: Which developmental event most likely explains these nodules?

options.A: Failure of the vitelline duct to involute
options.B: Unfused splenic buds in the dorsal mesogastrium
options.C: Incomplete fusion of the dorsal and ventral pancreatic buds
options.D: Fusion of splenic tissue with the descending gonad

whyNot.A: Gives a **Meckel diverticulum** on the ileum, holding gastric or pancreatic tissue, not **splenic** tissue at the **hilum**
whyNot.C: Gives **pancreas divisum**; it does not form **splenic** nodules
whyNot.D: Splenogonadal fusion leaves splenic tissue by the **testis or in the pelvis**; these nodules lie at the **splenic hilum**
whyNot.E: Gives an **indirect inguinal hernia or hydrocele**, not **splenic** nodules

answer: Accessory spleens: splenic mesenchymal buds in the dorsal mesogastrium that failed to fuse
why: The spleen forms in the 5th week from **mesenchymal buds in the dorsal mesogastrium**, which normally **fuse** into one organ as it moves to the left upper quadrant. A bud that **fails to fuse** becomes an **accessory spleen**, most often at the **splenic hilum**. With **no trauma or surgery**, splenosis is not the explanation.

idea.rule: Spleen = mesoderm of the dorsal mesogastrium (not foregut endoderm); unfused buds form accessory spleens.
also: Most accessory spleens lie at the splenic hilum
The splenic bud lies near the urogenital ridge, so splenic tissue can fuse with a gonad (splenogonadal fusion)
An accessory spleen left after splenectomy can cause ITP or hemolysis to relapse
The spleen is supplied by the celiac trunk although it is not a foregut derivative
